To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the accuracy of global tide model surface elevations is improved by (1) using a realistic bathymetry and (2) using a realistic parameterization of abyssal drag.

the optimal tuning factor in a forward model with topographic drag is nearly the same whether one-layer or two-layer dynamics are used, and that the optimal tuning factors for the baroclinic and barotropic tides are nearly identical.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of forward numerical solutions for the global barotropic tide.
the accuracy of global forward tide models, and not with the accuracy of inverse models.
the accuracy of global barotropic and global barotropic plus baroclinic numerical models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
baroclinic dynamics are necessary to obtain accurate global tide models, but are not sufficient, because of the need to account for the drag of waves breaking on topography.
the baroclinic tidal solution is not significantly more accurate than the barotropic solution in the present context.
the two-layer model is not superior to the one-layer model in forward tide modeling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a one-layer model with optimally tuned topographic drag and abyssal drag is sufficient to obtain accurate global barotropic tides, while the inclusion of baroclinicity in the two-layer solution improves accuracy in deep waters.

, for the present generation of global bathymetric datasets, the accuracy of forward barotropic tide models is limited by uncertainties in the drag coefficient, and that the accuracy of barotropic tide models can be improved by using a tuned drag parameterization that concentrates drag over rough topographic features.
a global numerical model of the barotropic tide can be made accurate by tuning a parameterized drag scheme, but that the baroclinic tidal model is not significantly better.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of forward models of the global tide is not as good as is often assumed, even when the model includes a realistic treatment of the baroclinic effects.
forward global tide simulations can be accurate if a realistic drag parameterization is used.
the accuracy of forward models is not improved significantly by baroclinic dynamics unless the barotropic component is already accurate.
